prompt: Send configurable reminder emails to customers with abandoned carts based on delay and frequency settings.

intent.desiredOutcome: Send configurable reminder emails to customers with abandoned carts based on delay and frequency settings.
intent.qualityBrief: A good version handles edge cases: respects customer opt-out preferences where possible, avoids sending duplicate emails in the same batch, tracks which carts have already received how many emails, and stops sending once the max is reached. The admin page should show clear, readable logs of sent emails with customer names and cart values so merchants can see what's working. Common pitfall: sending the same email multiple times in quick succession if the cron job runs too frequently without proper state tracking.

plan.dataFlow: Every ten minutes the scheduler fetches all abandoned carts from the external platform and, for each cart, checks whether a reminder record already exists; new carts are inserted as pending. For each pending or active cart, the system computes whether the configured delay since abandonment (or since the last send) has elapsed and whether the maximum send count has not been reached. Carts whose customer has opted out of marketing are immediately marked suppressed and skipped. Eligible carts receive a reminder email, and the send is recorded in the audit log while the cart reminder row is advanced to active and its send count incremented. Once the send count reaches the configured maximum, the cart is marked completed and no further emails are sent.

triggers.jobPurpose: Identify abandoned carts due for a reminder email and dispatch those emails within configured limits.
triggers.perTickWork: Fetch all recently abandoned carts, evaluate each against delay and frequency settings, send reminder emails to eligible carts, and persist the outcome for every cart processed.

capabilities.description: Retrieve all currently abandoned carts from the platform, including customer contact information and cart value.
Verify whether each cart's customer has opted out of marketing communications.
Load the merchant's configured initial delay, inter-email frequency, and maximum send count.
Determine, for each tracked cart, whether enough time has elapsed since abandonment or last send and the send limit has not been reached.
Deliver a personalised abandoned-cart reminder email to the customer.
Persist the result of a send attempt, increment the cart's send count, and advance the cart reminder to its next state.
Create a new cart reminder row for a newly discovered abandoned cart, or confirm an existing one is already tracked.
Mark a cart reminder as suppressed when the customer has opted out of marketing, recording the reason.
Return a paginated list of reminder send records for display in the merchant admin panel.
dataNeeds: send count at time of send

capabilities.description: Persist updated merchant configuration for delay, frequency, and maximum email count.

transitions.trigger: subsequent reminder email successfully sent within the maximum limit
customer opted out of marketing before any send
customer opted out of marketing after at least one send

invariants: A cart in the completed state never receives another reminder email
A cart in the suppressed state never receives another reminder email
Exactly one cart_reminders row exists per cart external identifier
The send_count on a cart_reminders row always equals the number of successful send records in reminder_sends for that cart
send_count never exceeds max_sends_per_cart at the moment of any send attempt

externalContracts.purpose: Return the current reminder configuration so the merchant can review delay, frequency, and send limit values.
Save updated reminder configuration values supplied by the merchant.
Return a paginated list of reminder send records showing customer name, email, cart value, send time, and outcome for merchant review.

edgeCases: A cart is discovered on two consecutive ticks before the first send is committed — the upsert must be idempotent so only one reminder row is created and only one email is dispatched.
A customer's email address is absent from the cart payload — the cart reminder is created as suppressed immediately with the reason recorded, and no send is attempted.

The merchant reduces max_sends_per_cart below the send count already recorded for some active carts — those carts must be transitioned to completed on the next tick without sending an additional email.

The scheduler tick duration exceeds the cadence interval, causing overlapping runs — each tick must check last_sent_at and send_count atomically before dispatching to prevent double-sends in the same window.
A customer opts out of marketing between two reminder sends — the opt-out check runs at the start of each tick, so the cart is suppressed before the next send regardless of elapsed time.

The external platform returns a cart that was subsequently purchased before the email is sent — the reminder email is still dispatched since purchase status is not tracked; merchants should be informed this is expected behaviour and use cart recovery conversion metrics to assess impact.

hld_v_findings.issue: The second trigger declares kind 'inbound-request' but provides no path, purpose, requestShape, or linked capabilities, making it impossible to implement and leaving LLD engineers with no specification for what this surface is supposed to do.
hld_v_findings.fix: Either remove the stub trigger entirely if the admin HTTP surface is already covered by externalContracts, or fully specify path, method, purpose, and which capabilities it invokes.

hld_v_findings.issue: No edge case covers email delivery failure from the 'send-reminder-email' notify capability — the plan has no signal for LLD on whether a failed send should leave the cart_reminders row in its prior state, be retried on the next tick, or be recorded as a failed attempt that still increments no send_count, creating an ambiguous failure path.
hld_v_findings.fix: Add an edge case specifying that when the email integration returns a failure the send attempt is written to reminder_sends with outcome 'failed', send_count is not incremented, and the cart remains in its current state so the next tick re-evaluates eligibility.

hld_v_findings.issue: The 'list-email-logs' capability's dataNeeds omit pagination inputs (page, page_size) that are declared on the corresponding GET /admin/logs route, so the capability spec gives no signal to LLD that the underlying query must accept and honour limit/offset parameters.
hld_v_findings.fix: Add 'page number' and 'page size' to the dataNeeds of list-email-logs to make the pagination contract visible at the capability level.
